items.title: Cauvery dispute: SC directs Karnataka to comply with CWMA order, seeks release status
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday, August 17, directed the Karnataka government to comply with the Cauvery Water Management Authority’s (CWMA) directions on releasing water to Tamil Nadu and sought a status report on the releases. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta was hearing Tamil Nadu’s plea seeking implementation of the CWMA’s directions. The Court posted the matter for August 24. Senior Advocate CS Vaidyanathan, appearing for Tamil Nadu, told the Court that Karnataka was not complying with the CWMA’s directions. He said Tamil Nadu had received only 14 TMC of water against the 64 TMC it was entitled to under the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal award. Vaidyanathan said Karnataka’s reservoirs had 76% live storage as of Monday morning and argued that, even after accounting for the deficit in inflows this year, Tamil Nadu should have received 55.29% of the mandated quantity. This, he said, left a backlog of around 20 TMC. Appearing for Karnataka, senior advocate Shyam Divan disputed the allegation of non-compliance and said the state was facing “extremely severe distress” in the Cauvery basin.
